prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: knee injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1417; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this matter.

Q: Understood. Let's start with the accident. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was in Sugar Land, Texas, at an intersection near a shopping center. I was driving a sedan and making a left turn across the opposing lanes.

Q: What was the traffic signal doing when you began your turn?
A: The light had turned yellow and I judged I had time to clear the intersection. I did have a green arrow, though, so I believed I had the right of way.

Q: And what happened next?
A: A pickup coming from the other direction struck the passenger side of my car. I felt a hard impact and the airbag deployed. My knee hit the dashboard.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
A: No. I was dazed for a few seconds, but I stayed conscious and got out of the car on my own.

Q: Let's talk about the knee. When did you first notice pain?
A: Right away. It was swollen within an hour, and by evening I couldn't bend it past a certain point without sharp pain.

Q: Who treated you after the accident?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They took X-rays and referred me to an orthopedic doctor for an MRI and follow-up visits.

Q: Have you had physical therapy?
A: Yes. I have attended sessions twice a week for several months. The therapist works on range of motion and strengthening.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the knee?
A: I missed several days early on because I couldn't stand for long periods. Now I work at a desk most of the time, but I still have to get up and move every half hour or so.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Stairs are hard. I used to jog a few mornings a week and I've stopped completely. Grocery shopping takes longer because I have to rest. I also can't kneel in the garden like I used to, which I miss.

Q: Do you still have pain today?
A: Yes, especially after I've been on my feet for a while or when the weather changes. Some days are better than others.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that same knee?
A: Not that I can recall. I played recreational soccer many years ago, but I never had a knee problem serious enough to see a doctor for it.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you would like to add to your answers?
A: No, I think I've covered it. I just want to get back to normal.
